comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 continuity check; complete official curriculum table 2025-2026
comparator.sourceNotes: The current LUMC programme page and 2026-2027 Year 1 timetable confirm an active three-year Biomedical Sciences bachelor and the same first-year sequence. Live 2026-2027 Leiden module endpoints confirm the names and credits of nearly all substantive first- and second-year courses, including Immunology, Infectious Agents and Immunity, Design and Analysis of Biomedical Studies, Physiology, Hormones and the Nervous System and Human Pathology. Leiden's latest complete accessible official curriculum table is the 2025-2026 Study Guide; it accounts for exactly 180 EC and supplies the integrated skills lines and third-year allocations that are not exposed by the new live catalogue. This reconstruction preserves that exact 60+60+60 structure and records the one-year source-continuity limitation explicitly rather than inventing changes. No formal route is selected: Year 3 contains a genuine 15-EC elective or half-minor space.
components: Design and Analysis of Biomedical Studies
Compulsory independent biomedical research project and final work.

core: Human biology from molecules and cells to tissues, organs and the whole body
Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, cell signalling and genomics
Mechanisms, causes, diagnosis, prevention and treatment of human disease
Immunology, medical microbiology and infectious disease
Experimental, laboratory and independent biomedical research
Epidemiology, biostatistics, biomedical data and research design
adjacent: Molecular diagnostics, therapeutic development and translation to clinical care
Disease prevention, public health, medical ethics and communication
questions: How do healthy and diseased human bodies function from molecules to organs?
How can genetic, cellular, immunological and experimental methods explain disease mechanisms?
How can biomedical evidence support prevention, diagnosis and improved treatment?

alternatives.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, anatomy and physiology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and neuroscience with laboratory, statistical and ethical study. It reflects Leiden's clinically oriented biomedical core while UCR lacks the complete wet-lab sequence and compulsory 21-EC research placement.
alternatives.labelReason: The official degree centres on the human body, disease mechanisms, molecular and cellular biology, microbiology, immunology, laboratory work and independent biomedical research.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Public health, disease prevention and biomedical intervention
alternatives.concept: Studies illness across body systems and populations, combining epidemiology, immunology, human physiology, health psychology, social conditions, health financing and research methods. The organising question shifts from laboratory mechanisms toward prevention and evaluation of interventions.
alternatives.labelReason: Prevention, translation to healthcare and Patient Oriented Research provide a direct basis for a population-level health and intervention programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses differ from the biomedical core route, adding sociology, health psychology, qualitative research, public economics and persuasion while reducing specialist neuroscience, anatomy and mathematical/computational methods.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Biomedical data, diagnostics and disease models
alternatives.concept: Connects cellular and physiological disease study with programming, mathematical modelling, image analysis, machine learning and neural networks. These are general UCR computational methods applied to biomedical questions, not a substitute for Leiden's laboratory training, molecular diagnostics or Student Research Project.
alternatives.labelReason: The programme's distinctive omics and systems-biology line, genome analysis, biomedical statistics, data science and personalised-treatment questions support a quantitative biomedical route.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses differ from the closest biomedical route and twelve from public health: image processing, deep learning, linear algebra, numerical methods and signal systems displace several pharmacology, neurobehavioral and clinical research elements, materially changing the analytical tools.
progression: Every course meets Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability, formal prerequisite order and the six-semester workload. Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods where required. Advisory progression was reviewed.

selection.assessment: The broad closest route covers human biology, molecular disease mechanisms and biomedical research. Direct target evidence then supports distinct public-health/intervention and biomedical-data/diagnostics alternatives. All three form coherent 24-course curricula, pass mechanical feasibility and differ by at least four courses per side. Production stops at the maximum of three.

notes.text: Leiden Biomedical Sciences requires a tightly integrated molecular, physiological, clinical, immunological and laboratory sequence, followed by a 21-EC Student Research Project and 15 EC of elective or half-minor space. UCR can assemble biomedical, public-health and quantitative-data programmes, but it does not duplicate Leiden's complete wet-lab sequence, clinical orientation or guaranteed research placement; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than equivalence.
